description: The hydrogen hub planned from a projected H2 demand: the offtake grows 10 → 18 → 25 MW over 2027, 2030 and 2035 beside a 40 MW process load on a 200 MW connection. Wind, solar, battery and electrolyser candidates per period. Multi-period; tagged for an Energy Hub study.

ledger.note: the solve discounts each period's costs at it
held flat to the base year, then escalated from it at the case's rates; nothing is converted with a price index
ledger.value: pack prices (2025 EUR) are read as real base-year EUR

ledger.note: pre-tax; a later stage's capex is paid a year before its COD
ledger.value: nominal EUR, escalation 2 %/yr, all equity at 7 %, close 2026-01-01, to 2045

ledger.note: the customer's demand ramp; replace with the offtake contract
not modelled, so the counterfactual bill is the served load at the meter
an illustrative network-use charge on top of the wholesale price; synthetic, illustrative; no money year of its own; read in the case's money (2025)
the 2027 offtake (10 MW of H2) needs about 15 MW; the plan adds the rest by period as the offtake grows
each period is one representative week standing for several years, so no energy is carried from one period into the next
the pack's fuel cell lives 10 years: a staged one would retire before 2045
ledger.value: the existing 10 MW unit, no staged candidate

ledger.note: the investment-case route re-solves the hub without the candidates, with a grey-H2 supply at the reference price plus that period's CO2
ledger.value: compared with the hub as it stands today, buying grey H2 whenever that is cheaper than running its electrolyser

ledger.note: synthetic demo value, in the case's base-year (2027) money, escalating 2 %/yr as fuel; a real study uses the site's SMR supply contract and its certified carbon intensity

synthetic demo path, real prices in 2020 money, converted at the case's 2 % inflation (the case is nominal); applied to the grey-H2 purchase only; a real study uses the ETS forward curve or a stated policy path
grid imports carry no CO2 cost, so the avoided CO2 is the grey-H2 purchase's alone
the campus run's island checks and the report's islanding chapter read it
ledger.value: seamless: the batteries form the island and carry the 40 MW process load; no genset, no UPS

ledger.note: demo values copied from the data center and gridspine, not from a datasheet or a grid code
ledger.value: batteries: the data center's bess_new block (droop 4 %, tau_f 0.1 s, i_max 1.2 pu, k_gfm_min 1.0, pf 0.95); fuel cell, wind and PV: gridspine's drafted grid-following default (Q(U), pf 0.95); the data center's frequency limits; sustained 1 h, bridge 600 s

ledger.note: the plan is not sized to island; turn them on to plan for islanding. Measured on this plan (electrolysis priced per MW of electrical input, GS-2b, 2026-10-21): at 1 h sustained they add about 43 MW of battery in 2027, hold the grid import to about 3 MW and take the demo NPV from -2.6 M to -30.5 M EUR; at 4 h the NPV is -51.9 M EUR; at 24 h no plan meets them (owner: island data on, rows off, the user opts in)

ledger.label: Connection ramp limit
ledger.note: assumed: 10% of the 200 MW connection per minute; RfG/DCC set no ramp limit for a demand facility, so this is a placeholder of the order a network operator writes into a connection offer for large loads

ledger.label: Power oscillation limit
ledger.note: assumed: peak-to-peak power oscillation at most 1 % of the connection in the 0.1-2 Hz band (forced-oscillation concern for large loads, NERC 2025 large-loads white paper); no code value

ledger.label: Import efficiency
ledger.note: assumed: the grid_import Link's efficiency (losses = 1 - efficiency); what reaches the site side of the PoC Link. Losses further in (transformers, UPS) are not in it

ledger.label: Fault level at the PoC
ledger.note: assumed: short-circuit power at the PoC (grid); the SCR and rapid-voltage-change screenings read it

provenance: synthetic illustrative data (P19 template) — representative week, public-catalogue-range costs; replace with project data before any decision
study_notes: Each period is the same representative week, with the period's H2 offtake.
Candidates are one row per period (build_year = the period): the plan says what to build when.
After a solve the investment case compares the plan with the hub as it stands today, which buys grey H2 (synthetic demo price and CO2 path) whenever that is cheaper than running its electrolyser.
The connection (200 MW) carries the grid-only site in every period.
Island rows are off: the plan is not sized to island; the island checks report what islanding would need.
